key_insight: A SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar cell stacks and pinpoint the most influential layer properties for high-efficiency designs.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical screening framework for selecting ETL, absorber, and HTL combinations, including lead-free double perovskites, to accelerate architecture optimization before full device simulation or fabrication.
method: Simulated 125 ETL/absorber/HTL device architectures with SCAPS-1D
Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unseen stacks
Used SHAP to identify the dominant design descriptors and verify top candidates with full simulations
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed strong ranking performance, and the workflow identified validated devices reaching 28.85% PCE for FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag and 28.62% for FTO/SnO2/Cs2AgInBr6/NiO/Ag.
watch_item: Predictions depend on the quality and coverage of the simulated training space, so transfer to new materials or fabrication conditions may require retraining and experimental validation.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
